clue.text: Drop a note when in difficulty

parts.note: to drop a plan is to scrap it
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A singer in trouble lets a note fall flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In difficulty' reads as one phrase, but only 'difficulty' is the definition: being in a scrape is being in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament or tight spot, as in getting into a scrape with the law.

clue.text: It's to be found in the estate agent's brochure

definitions.text: It's to be found in the estate agent's brochure

parts.words: It's to be found in the estate agent's brochure
parts.note: surface reading: some feature of a property listed in a sales leaflet
setter's reading: a verb meaning to place or locate

explanation.surface: Something you would spot in a house-seller's glossy leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: Estate agents traditionally write the old participle form, as in 'a cottage situate near the green', so the word itself is found in their brochures.
explanation.definitionFit: To situate something is to place or locate it, which is where it is 'to be found'.

clue.text: Make master, finally, a head

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the final letter of master
so much a head means so much each

explanation.surface: An instruction to promote a schoolmaster to headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make master' looks like a phrase about promotion, but 'Make' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a place, as in 'we made the summit by noon', is to arrive at or get to it.

clue.text: Turns up in chilly surroundings yet well received

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for chilly
surroundings shows the chilly word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: polar regions are icy cold

indicators.note: turns tells us the word that follows is flipped to run the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone appears in a cold setting and still gets a warm welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns up' reads as 'arrives', but the two words split: one flips the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something popular is liked and approved by many people, which is to say well received.

clue.text: Big run on a famous Swiss bank

definitions.text: Big run on a famous Swiss bank

parts.words: Big run on a famous Swiss bank
parts.note: surface reading: a panic in which customers rush to withdraw money from a Swiss bank

parts.words: run on a famous Swiss bank
parts.note: setter's reading: a toboggan course carved down a snowy slope in St Moritz, Switzerland

explanation.surface: Depositors stampede to withdraw their savings from a well-known Zurich bank.
explanation.walkthrough: A run on a bank is a rush of withdrawals; here the run is an ice track and the bank is a snowy slope.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cresta Run is the celebrated toboggan course at St Moritz in the Swiss Alps.

clue.text: A car's crashed and left by villain

indicators.note: a crashed vehicle is smashed out of shape, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, with the s of the possessive
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A villain wrecks a car and abandons it at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a rogue or scoundrel, a mild word for a wrongdoer or knave.

clue.text: Graphic new form of catechism

indicators.note: a new form of a word is the same letters made into a different shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A church's question-and-answer teaching gets a modern illustrated version.
explanation.definitionFit: A schematic drawing presents something as a diagram, so it is graphic in the sense of shown in pictures.

clue.text: Stimulated to use a rod, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is spurred into action by a fishing rod or a cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Aroused means excited or stirred up, which is what stimulated means as a past participle.

clue.text: Cheap transport

parts.note: surface reading: a low-cost way of getting about, like a bargain bus fare
setter's reading: a vehicle named after two of the smallest old British coins

explanation.walkthrough: The penny and the farthing (a quarter of a penny) were old British coins of tiny value, so the Victorian high-wheeled bicycle named after them sounds as cheap as transport gets.
explanation.definitionFit: The penny-farthing is an early bicycle with one huge front wheel and one small rear wheel, a means of transport.

clue.text: A feature of Sicily and French North Africa

parts.note: et is French for and
N for North and A for Africa

explanation.surface: A geography question about the Mediterranean: Sicily, France and North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a link joining two places, but 'and French' asks for the French word for and.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano dominating eastern Sicily, its most famous landmark.

clue.text: Educational institution where homework comes before discipline?

indicators.note: comes before fixes the order, putting the homework word at the front

parts.note: prep is British school slang for homework, short for preparation
to school someone is to train or discipline them

explanation.surface: A school whose rule is that homework must be done before any punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a prep school is a private school preparing children, usually up to 13, for senior school.
explanation.definitionFit: A prep school is a private fee-paying school for younger pupils, so it is a place of learning.

clue.text: She has pain from one side to the other

parts.note: R for right, one side
an ache is a dull pain
L for left, the other side

explanation.surface: A woman whose pain spreads right across her body.
explanation.walkthrough: The pain runs from right to left, so it sits between the two side letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachel is a woman's name, and crosswords often define a girl's name simply as she.

clue.text: Mean error puts it just off target

parts.note: near is old-fashioned British for stingy or mean with money
a miss is a failure or mistake

explanation.surface: A statistician's average deviation explains why the shot narrowly missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean error' looks like a statistics term, but each word works on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is a shot or attempt that narrowly fails to hit what it aimed for.

clue.text: How seasick people feel on disembarking?

definitions.text: How seasick people feel on disembarking?

parts.words: How seasick people feel on disembarking?
parts.note: surface reading: the relief of queasy passengers stepping onto dry land
setter's reading: improved once they are off the ship, which is also a phrase for richer

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means more prosperous, but literally it says the sufferers feel better once they are off the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Better off means in a more favourable position, usually wealthier, but here simply happier ashore.

clue.text: But for this, life would be unbearable

definitions.text: But for this, life would be unbearable

parts.words: But for this, life would be unbearable
parts.note: surface reading: some comfort or joy that makes existence worth living
setter's reading: unbearable literally means not able to be borne, so the thing missing is the capacity to put up with things

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a sentimental line about love or hope; the precise opposite of unbearable is something we can bear, and the quality needed is endurance of others.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is the ability to bear or put up with hardship and other people, making things bearable.

clue.text: Boss seen in a boiled shirt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a raised knob or ornamental ... on a surface
second meaning: the fastener pushed through a stiff dress shirt

explanation.surface: The company chief spotted wearing a stiff evening shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A boiled shirt is a starched formal dress shirt, fastened with detachable studs. 'Boss' suggests the manager but means a knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is both a decorative knob or boss and a button-like fastener for a dress shirt.

clue.text: Boring makers of laws

parts.note: taken as written; the same four letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A dig at tedious legislators: lawmakers are dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makers of laws' reads as politicians; split it after 'makers' and the tools that make holes are spelt with the letters of the last word, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes, so awls are things that make bores.

clue.text: Used when a path's relaid round top of the lane

definitions.text: Used when a path's relaid round top of the lane

indicators.note: round says these letters go on either side of the other piece
something relaid is put down again in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, with the s of the possessive

indicators.note: the top of a word written down the grid is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of lane

explanation.surface: Road surfacing material used when a footpath near the lane is resurfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the material, and its wordplay also builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarry surfacing material laid on roads and paths when they are resurfaced.

clue.text: A cottager going out may wear it

definitions.text: A cottager going out may wear it

indicators.note: going out suggests the letters leave their places and wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A villager pulls on something warm before heading outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, while its first three words also supply and signal the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a heavy overcoat, exactly what a country dweller might put on before stepping outside.

clue.text: Leave a bar with a university man

parts.note: taken as written
to bar something is to ban it
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a pub with an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave a bar' suggests quitting a pub; 'bar' is a verb meaning prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon something is to leave it behind for good, deserting it.

clue.text: Question one about point that's not straightforward

parts.note: to ask is to question

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for one encloses the point

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice
N for north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Interrogating someone about a matter that seems devious.
explanation.walkthrough: Looking askance is looking sideways, with suspicion; the definition describes that indirect manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Askance means sideways or obliquely, so a look given askance is indirect rather than direct.

clue.text: Capital city — the big smoke?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the capital of Cuba
second meaning: a large cigar, named after that city

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Big Smoke' is a nickname for London, which pulls towards the wrong capital; here the smoke is a fat cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana is the capital of Cuba and also the name of a premium Cuban cigar.

clue.text: Proposal made by pilots before landing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an overture or suggestion put to someone
second meaning: the final flight path towards a runway

explanation.surface: Pilots put forward a suggestion before the aircraft touches down.
explanation.definitionFit: An approach is both an overture to someone and the descending path an aircraft flies to a runway.

clue.text: Naturally cold state, but sweet when baked

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the icy northernmost US state
second meaning: the dessert of ice cream in meringue, browned in the oven

explanation.surface: A frozen territory that turns delicious after time in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: Baked Alaska is ice cream and sponge covered in meringue and briefly baked.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the frigid US state, and baked Alaska is a well-known hot-and-cold pudding.

clue.text: Last word to the French about to expire

definitions.text: Last word to the French about to expire

parts.words: Last word to the French about to expire
parts.note: surface reading: a final remark addressed to French people who are dying
setter's reading: a farewell in French, which a dying person might say

explanation.walkthrough: The French farewell, literally 'to God', is a fitting final word for someone near death, and it even has DIE in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French for goodbye, used in English for a final farewell.

clue.text: Made claim that was upheld

definitions.meaning: second meaning: kept up or preserved in good order

explanation.surface: A claim was lodged and the court supported it.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain is both to assert firmly that something is true and to keep something in good condition.

clue.text: Pubs names one's made a case for

indicators.note: a case holds things, so the first piece encloses the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, plus the s of the possessive
N is the abbreviation for name, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Pubs whose names someone argues in favour of keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a case for' sounds like arguing in support, but means forming a casing around.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub or tavern, often one that also offers rooms to travellers.

clue.text: Despicable person possibly got time inside

indicators.note: inside puts the word for time within the rearranged letters
possibly hints that the next word may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A contemptible person who may well have been sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got time inside' reads as served a prison sentence. A toerag is British slang for a nasty, worthless person.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerag is a British insult for a contemptible or worthless individual, a lowlife.

clue.text: Put up with being last

definitions.meaning: second meaning: survive or continue for a long time

explanation.surface: Tolerating the indignity of coming in at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective meaning final; it is the verb meaning go on.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is both to tolerate hardship and to persist or survive over time.
